rappel_detail.notes: Lands at trees on a gentler snow patch.
rappel_detail.anchor: large tree with 2 slings and 2 rings

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel to the base.

current.descent_text: Rappel from a large tree with slings and rings at the top of the route onto a gentler snowy patch with more trees, then rappel again to the base.

rappel_detail.notes: Reaches the other fixed rappel anchor on the ledge.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed rappel anchor at top of pitch 5

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel directly down from the ledge to the bolted anchor of a summer sport climb.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed rappel anchor on the ledge

rappel_detail.notes: Two bolts; this rappel reaches the ground.
rappel_detail.anchor: 2 bolts on a summer sport route

current.descent_text: From the upper pitches you can walk off west down scree and talus. Otherwise rappel from the fixed anchor near the top of the fifth pitch to the ledge anchor, then straight down to the bolted anchor of a summer sport route, which reaches the ground.

rappel_detail.notes: Downclimb from the summit to the anchor, then rappel into the east gully to a big tree.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed anchor just below the summit

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel off a big tree in the gully.
Rappel off another big tree.
Rappel off another big tree.
Last rappel off a tree, reaching the base.

current.descent_text: Downclimb to the fixed anchor just under the summit and rappel from there to a big tree standing in the east gully. From then on, rappel from further big trees down that gully to the base.

rappel_detail.notes: Carry 8 to 10 ft of cord or sling for the horn; sun damage wears it out each season. Double ropes are preferred. Rappelling east lands on the top of pitch 1.
Second rappel on the east side reaches the ground.

current.descent_text: Belay from the horn on top of the cirque crest, which is also the rappel anchor, so carry a length of cord or sling for it. You can rappel either east or west; on the east side, the first rappel reaches the top of the first pitch and the next reaches the ground.

rappel_detail.notes: Double-rope rappel from the top of the route. Keep one rope end fixed at the bottom of pitch 5, otherwise you cannot get back to the face and end up hanging in space.
Double-rope rappel to bolts on a steep face above a ledge, 50 m straight down and to the right of the route.
Double-rope rappel to the bolts passed halfway through pitch 1.

Single-rope rappel to the ground. Alternatively, from the base of pitch 5 rappel 30 m to the base of pitch 4 (swing left to reach it), then a double-rope rappel to the top of pitch 1, then one to the ground.

current.descent_text: Rappelling the route is the best way down; the rappels use double ropes, stopping at the triangular tower at the base of the fifth pitch and at the bolts passed halfway up the first pitch.

rappel_detail.notes: A short rappel to the top of pitch 4. Leave a rope tied at the pitch 4 anchor so you can pull yourself back into the belay; it is steeper than it looks.
Long double-rope rappel to the top of pitch 2.
Double-rope rappel; anchor cord and a carabiner were left in place.
Last double-rope rappel to the ground. Another option is to walk across the summit to the standard rappel stations on the southeast side of Lion's Head.

current.descent_text: With a full wall kit, rappel the route, using a long double-rope rappel to the top of the second pitch. The other option is to walk across the summit area to the usual rappel stations on Lion's Head's southeast side.

name: Bite the pillow, we're going in dry

rappel_detail.notes: One rappel to the base using two 80 m ropes.

current.descent_text: The route tops out on a ledge with webbing and rap rings, which are used to rappel back to the base.

name: Middle Peak via South Face - South Chimney

current.rappels: 2 x 60 ft (18m) rappels down the South Chimney

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2, about 60 ft, down the South Chimney.
rappel_detail.station: The top of the South Chimney, at the summit of the Middle Peak.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2, about 60 ft, to the south-facing ledge below the rock gable. Then traverse back toward the Main-Middle notch and descend the talus.
rappel_detail.station: Partway down the South Chimney, at the end of the first rappel.

current.descent_text: From the summit, set up two sequential 60-ft (18m) rappels down the South Chimney to regain the south-facing ledge below the rock gable. From there, downclimb/traverse back toward the Main-Middle notch area and descend the talus slope, retracing the brushy off-trail section and the Mineral Creek trail back to the trailhead and river ford.
